行.meaning: On the left a <part>chairlift</part> rattles past; on the right stands a signpost with two arms and a hooked foot. Together they make a busy <part>crossroads</part> where nobody stops: skiers jump off the chairlift and keep <kanji>going</kanji>, left, right or straight on.
行.on: Every skier grabs an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne at the crossroads and eats it on the move.
行.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals a skier as the chairlift tips her off, and away she goes down the slope.

子.meaning: A round little head, arms flung out wide, one hooked leg kicking at the floor: someone tiny is in the middle of a tantrum. They will not eat their peas. It's a <kanji>child</kanji>.
子.on: The child hides behind a toy <sound>shi</sound>eld and throws the peas over the top.
子.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala climbs onto the child's back and won't let go.

女.meaning: A figure flings her arms out and bends her knees low, legs crossed, balancing on one foot. She holds the pose for a whole minute while the crowd claps and the judges gasp. She's a <kanji>woman</kanji> with very strong legs.
女.on: A <sound>jo</sound>gger runs laps around her the whole time, trying to make her wobble.
女.kun: <sound>On</sound>ly she can balance a stack of <sound>na</sound>an on her head while standing on one foot.

今.meaning: An <part>umbrella</part> pops open over a <part>one</part>-plank bench, and a little zigzag of lightning strikes the ground right under it. The storm starts this very second. Don't wait: get under it <kanji>now</kanji>!
今.on: A giant <sound>con</sound>dor swoops down and squeezes under the umbrella with you.
今.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k! <sound>Ma</sound>, now!' yells the kid, diving under the umbrella as the lightning strikes.

食.meaning: Under an <part>umbrella</part> roof sits a bowl of steaming white rice with a spoon stuck in it. Rain pours down all around, but nobody cares: you sit under the umbrella and <kanji>eat</kanji> every grain.
食.on: Every time the chef tastes the stew, his hair springs straight up in a wild <sound>shock</sound>.
食.kun: Rice finished, you start on a crunchy <sound>ta</sound>co, still under the umbrella.

口.meaning: A tiny square <part>cage</part> with nothing inside sits on the table. Then it opens and closes, opens and closes, and starts asking for snacks. It was never a cage at all: it's a <kanji>mouth</kanji>.
口.on: The mouth gulps down a whole ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne in one bite.
口.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the mouth, holding a lump of <sound>chee</sound>se.

何.meaning: Next to a <part>coat hook</part> hangs an <part>approval</part> sign: a mouth under a little shelf that says yes to everything. Hang a hat on the hook, and the mouth nods. Hang a dripping fish on it, and the mouth finally frowns: '<kanji>What</kanji>? What is that thing?'
何.on: A <sound>ca</sound>rp flops out from behind the shelf. 'What? What is a fish doing here?'
何.kun: 'What's for dinner?' asks the mouth. Just <sound>naan</sound>, a flat bread as wide as the shelf.
